posts.author: trendyvers
youralphamom
posts.text:
Veo 3.1 vs Gemini Omni Flash vs Grok Imagine 1.5 vs Seedance 2.0 — a new battle for the best AI video generator.

I tested all 4 models with the same difficult action prompt.

Quick note: this was not a strict one-shot test. The prompt was complex, so I gave each model up to 4 attempts max.

Here’s what happened:

Veo 3.1 — weak result, which was honestly expected at this point.

Gemini Omni Flash — surprisingly decent, but only on the 4th attempt.

Grok Imagine 1.5 — the new hyped release looked pretty weak here. On the 4th attempt, it finally beat Veo, but it was still far behind Seedance 2.0 and Gemini Omni Flash on this task.

Seedance 2.0 — nailed it on the 1st attempt. I tried a second generation too, but the first one was better. Best physics, best tension, best overall action feel.

My current ranking:

1. Seedance 2.0 — still the leader
2. Gemini Omni Flash
3. Grok Imagine 1.5
4. Veo 3.1 — feels outdated now

For this kind of complex action scene, Seedance is still clearly ahead in my opinion.

What do you think? Which model won this round?

#AIVideo

posts.author: hodlreaper
posts.text:
Google's Gemini Omni Flash ran 6 edits on 1 photo before I called it serious

The pitch was conversational editing, so I stopped reading and started testing.

First, make a solid object see-through. It dropped the opacity and kept every edge of the original frame structure intact, nothing warped.

Then the easy one everyone has seen: swap an object out. 1 pass. So I pushed harder, dropped an animal into the room, reached over to pet it, and the model held the contact instead of melting the hand into fur.

Edit 4 is the post-production move most people actually want. The sofa was in the way, so I removed it. Empty floor, matched lighting, no smear where it sat.

Then the background. I animated it  the thing I had only seen in other testers' clips until I ran it myself. It moved.

Last, I swapped the water out and rebuilt the surface. 

That one needed the most prompting, but it landed.

6 tests, 6 passes. Not flawless a couple needed a second instruction, and it wants more abuse before I trust it on client work. But Google shipped this at I/O on May 19, and the floor is already this high.ʼ

6 clean edits from a tool that is 10 days old.

If you need a guide, let me know.

posts.author: juliangoldieseo
posts.text:
Google just dropped 6 AI tools at once.

Most people still think AI = chatbot. Big mistake.

Here’s what just changed:

→ Project Genie = build explorable 3D worlds from text

→ Gemini Omni = edit videos by talking instead of starting over

→ AI Studio Build Mode = build apps in plain English

→ Stitch = design websites by voice

→ Pix = create marketing graphics without design skills

→ Ask YouTube = get answers + jump to exact timestamps

The real shift?

Google is removing friction from workflows.

No coder.

No designer.

No editor.

Just describe what you want.

Save this video, you’ll understand where AI is actually heading.

posts.author: aimikoda
posts.text:
We used to do this with ControlNet back then. Wanted to try it with Gemini Omni.

Prompt: Use the provided logo as the master shape reference and create a 10-beat cinematic sequence where the logo appears in 10 different environments, mostly from top-down or aerial views. The logo should always be formed naturally by the scene itself, not as a flat overlay, with smooth seamless transitions connecting all beats into one flowing visual journey.

posts.author: codebypoonam
posts.text:
Google just made video editing as easy as texting.

Gemini Omni can:
→ Swap characters in your video
→ Change backgrounds instantly
→ Add or remove objects mid-scene
→ Manipulate camera angles
→ Create your own digital avatar with your voice
→ Apply cinematic zooms with one prompt
→ Reimagine existing landmarks entirely
→ Edit physics — gravity, fluid dynamics, kinetic energy
→ Build new worlds from a single instruction
→ Do all of this through a normal conversation
